source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
Harvest timing: harvest must be done on time to minimize post-harvest loss. The right time to harvest is when the grain hulls at the tip of the panicle have turned a straw-like yellow color and the grains have become firm/hard (no longer milky).

Selecting and saving seed for the next planting: let the seed-source rice fully ripen in the field (100% maturity) before harvesting it for seed. Dry the harvested seed down to about 14% moisture - the source notes this can be checked by biting a grain, which should break cleanly through the middle when dry enough. If freshly harvested grain at 18-25% moisture is stored right away without drying, it will spoil/rot from mold (fungi) and be attacked by storage insect pests, so grain must first be sun-dried for 2-3 days to bring it down to about 14% moisture before storage; over-drying should also be avoided, since excessively dried grain becomes prone to cracking and to breakage of the milled kernel during milling.

Seed storage: store the dried seed in sacks labeled with the variety name and the harvest date. Keep the stored seed in a clean location free of dust, away from sources of moisture, and with adequate ventilation (air circulation) around the stored sacks.
